newsitem.title: USA: SBC, PacTel call alternate merger proposal better.
newsitem.headline: SBC, PacTel call alternate merger proposal better.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc and Pacific Telesis Group said on Monday an alternate proposed decision on their planned merger by two California regulators was "a step in the right direction".
But the companies said the proposal by two members of the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) fell short "of what the record and CPUC precedent says should be done".
The CPUC is the only regulatory body whose approval is still required for the merger to go ahead.

CPUC commissioners Josiah Neeper and Richard Bilas proposed on Monday that the panel approve the $17 billion merger on condition that Pacific Telesis's Pacific Bell unit refund $248 million to ratepayers.
The proposed refund is less than half the $590.5 million which two administrative law judges said last month Pacific Bell should be required to refund. The judges make recommendations to the CPUC.
By the companies' calculations, the two commissioners' proposal called for more than $330 million in payments to California customers and other conditions.
The parties in the merger proceeding have 10 days to comment on the alternate proposed decision before the commission issues a final ruling, which is expected on March 31.

"We have some concerns with the alternate proposed decision because it fails to recognise the full extent of benefits this merger will bring to California," said Dick Odgers, Pacific Telesis executive vice-president and general counsel.
"While it's a step in the right direction and is much more reasonable than the administrative law judges' proposal, we do not believe that the payment to customers is warranted," he said.

The companies did not immediately comment on an alternative proposal by CPUC President Gregory Conlon that Pacific Bell be ordered to refund $315.67 million to customers over eight years as a condition for approval of the merger.
